source.description: Fixed vectors for symmetric primitives used by sealed sender in libsignal v0.99.1. libsignal's only fixed vector here is the AES-256-CTR unit test in rust/protocol/src/crypto.rs. That CTR mode starts from an all-zero 16-byte counter block and increments the last 4 bytes as a big-endian 32-bit counter; for inputs shorter than 2^32 blocks this equals ordinary AES-256-CTR with a zero 128-bit IV. Sealed sender v1 uses it, followed by a 10-byte truncated HMAC-SHA256, which this vector does not cover. The spec agent reproduced the ciphertext with 'openssl enc -aes-256-ctr' and a zero IV. Every other sealed-sender test upstream (v1 and v2 encrypt/decrypt, HKDF steps, AES-GCM-SIV) uses freshly generated keys and randomness, so no fixed end-to-end ciphertext exists upstream. Implementations should test v1/v2 by round trip, by these primitive vectors, and against captures from the reference binary.
